findings.title: Login and logout paths have unbounded steps and no failure-mode table
findings.description:
D7 defines three timeouts:
- `turn_timeout_s` covers `thread.run`.
- `login_timeout_s` covers only `handle.wait()`.
- `account_timeout_s` covers runtime start plus `account()`.

The Failure Modes table is scoped to "Codex Turn" and adds one login row (the `wait()` timeout). Several new I/O paths that spawn the runtime (line 82) are left out:

- **`sq auth logout`**: runtime start and `AsyncCodex.logout()` have no timeout key, no hang behavior, and no stated handling for an SDK error or transport close. A hung runtime hangs the command with no limit.
- **Login before `wait()`**: `AsyncCodex.__aenter__` and the `login_chatgpt()` / `login_chatgpt_device_code()` calls happen before the timeout starts. A runtime that never finishes `initialize` hangs `sq auth login` with no limit.
- **Extra missing on `sq auth login/logout`**: Success Criteria line 190 requires that any `openai-oauth` use without the extra fail with the install command. The design does not say where `login.py` or `OAuthFileStrategy.login` raise it, or what exit path they use. Only `create_agent` is named (line 122).
- **Transport closes mid-login**: there is no row saying the handle is cancelled and the runtime shut down, as the turn path does at lines 128-129.

Under the failure-mode rule, each of these needs an explicit, observable behavior and a test. Suggested fix: add a "Failure Modes — Login/Logout" table. Bounding runtime start, `login_chatgpt*()` and `logout()` with the existing `account_timeout_s` would cover the gaps without adding a new key.

findings.title: Alignment with the architecture's auth model is explicit and sound
findings.description:
`100-arch` says squadron does not unify authentication (arch line 243). The slice handles this directly:
- `InteractiveLogin` is an optional capability with one implementer.
- It hands the whole flow to the Codex runtime.
- Squadron stores no credentials; `~/.codex/auth.json` stays the only store.

Deferring the architecture text change until a second provider adopts the capability is the right size of response.

findings.title: Slice-plan scope fully covered, no scope cut
findings.description:
Every item in plan entry (129) maps to the design:
- **Part A:** the `openai_codex` port, bundled binary first with PATH as fallback, the `codex` extra, `ReasoningEffort` mapping (#171), and usage recording.
- **Part B:** the error naming the install command, the doctor row (package, binary, login state), the model-list marker, and the README.
- **Part C:** browser and device-code login, logout, and email/plan in status.

The exclusions (no squadron token store, no `login_api_key`) match the plan.

findings.title: Capability dispatch instead of profile-name checks
findings.description: D3 and D9 use `runtime_checkable` Protocols tested with `isinstance`. This respects slice 128's ban on string dispatch and ISP (API-key strategies don't have to stub login methods). The plan says "a capability on the strategy, not a profile-name check", and D3 does exactly that.

findings.title: Turn-path failure modes and silent-fallback removal
findings.description:
- **Turn path:** hang, timeout, transport close and teardown are each listed with observable behavior and a test per row.
- **D8:** removes `final_response or ""`, so an empty review can no longer reach the parser as a valid Message.
- **`OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback:** the open silent-fallback question is settled by a verification task with two defined outcomes (line 232), not left open.

findings.title: Lighter alternative to the new `ExtraRequirement` Protocol
findings.description: `ExtraRequirement` has one implementer and no planned consumer slice (frontmatter line 7). Because it is checked at runtime (`missing_extra_hint()`), it can't simply be a static `ProviderCapabilities` field, so a small Protocol is a reasonable choice. Even so, the "Provides to Other Slices" list (lines 179-181) describes reuse that nothing has planned yet. Keep the Protocol, but treat that list as speculative.

findings.title: Dependency on slice 931 is not in the slice-plan entry
findings.description: The plan lists `Dependencies: [128]`. The design also depends on 931 for `AgentConfig.effort`, `applies_effort` and `core/usage.py`. That dependency is real and correctly declared here. The plan entry could be updated to match.

findings.title: Version upper bound is stated and also called undecided
findings.description: D1 specifies `openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1`, but the same line and line 231 call the upper bound undecided. Either keep `<1` as the design's decision or drop it from the spec, so the task breakdown doesn't receive contradictory instructions. Also, D9 appears before D8 in the decision list (lines 112-114), which is cosmetic only.
